title: AI Coding Bill Explainer
oneLiner: A patient-facing receipt decoder that flags AI-documentation-driven coding complexity and prepares a calm billing question script.
targetUser: Privately insured patients, caregivers, and HR benefits helpers trying to understand higher medical bills.
keyUX: Paste a bill/EOB, classify confusing codes, compare visit story to billed complexity, generate safe questions, and assemble a billing call script.
sourceSignals: S7 - Healthcare Dive on AI documentation/coding as cost driver: https://www.healthcaredive.com/news/ai-push-healthcare-costs-higher-health-plans-say-pwc/822645/
stitchPrompt: Create a responsive web app called "AI Coding Bill Explainer" for privately insured patients, caregivers, and HR benefits helpers trying to understand higher medical bills. The app is based on observed user pull: patients already compare bills and EOBs, call billing departments, ask for coding reviews, and struggle with unfamiliar code language while health plans flag AI documentation and coding as a cost driver. The app should use a receipt decoder mechanic around the trigger moment "a confusing medical bill arrives after a visit" and make the first screen communicate "Question the code without sounding lost." Use the user's own language: "I need to ask whether this code is right without sounding like I am accusing anyone." Build the core workflow around bill lines, EOB details, visit date, diagnosis/procedure language, amount due, billing office contact, and due date, and produce a billing call script plus code-question checklist. Required sections: bill shock header, EOB and bill line parser, code complexity explainer cards, visit story vs billing language lane, ask-this/not-that script builder, insurer/provider call checklist, follow-up and due-date tracker, and shareable caregiver memo. Emotional pressure to make visible: 건강, overpayment fear, embarrassment about billing jargon, and deadline pressure before collections. Design direction: use the `financial-analyst` profile with off-white/graphite analytical panels, muted green confidence cues, precise tabular bill rows, restrained red warning states, 40px form controls, and no playful medical gimmicks. Avoid generic dashboard framing; make the main interaction feel like decoding one intimidating bill into three calm phone questions.
